title: ‘Botsitting’ puts the hidden labour of checking AI on the balance sheet
friendlyTitle: Checking AI work takes time, and businesses should count it
summary: An evidence-rich essay argues that AI productivity claims often omit the time workers spend supplying context, correcting mistakes and verifying outputs. It connects a 6,000-worker survey with human-factors research and a controlled developer study, while making a broader interpretation rather than presenting new primary research.
friendlySummary: Using AI also means explaining the task, fixing errors and checking the answer. This article brings together studies showing that this hidden work can use much of the time AI appears to save.
whyItMatters: Organizations should measure net completion time and accepted output, including review and rework, rather than prompts, seats or generation speed. If checking is essential, it needs an explicit owner, enough domain expertise and workload capacity—not a vague instruction to keep a human in the loop.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Measure how long it takes to finish correct work, including checks and fixes. Give review work enough time and a clear owner instead of pretending it is free.
